column3: Direct parallel: green sundus and brocade garments with bracelets frame the adorned garden as recompense.
A secondary resonance of blessings bestowed on believers, but it does not clarify the garments, bracelets, or drink.
Names the Lord in a paradisal setting; only a remote support for the direct divine attribution of the drink.
Parallels bracelets, adornment, and silk in gardens, supporting honored bodily ornament without requiring the same materials.
Immediately identifies the preceding scene as recompense and thanked striving, framing its outer adornment and drink as return.
Juxtaposes drinkable water and wearable ornament from the sea, linking nourishment and adornment as distinct divine benefits.
Directly repeats the sundus and brocade clothing, preserving the shared vision of elevated communal dress.
Begins the cup-mixture sequence that culminates in the Lord giving the purifying drink; mixture may also suggest inward effect.
Presents clothing as a contrary cover used to resist forgiveness, sharpening the difference between concealment and honored dress.
Supplies the silver vessels and circulating service immediately before the silver bracelets and final drink.
Links recompense to distinct worldly and final horizons; its work-return pattern supports, but does not define, the adornment.
Joins clothing and purification, supporting an outward-and-inward reading; a proposed recompense link remains contrastive rather than direct.
The contrary image of garments cut from fire and poured heat makes 76:21's clothing and drink a reversal of punitive enclosure.
Adds circulating everlasting attendants and pearl-like appearance, extending the visible service and radiance around 76:21.
Names seeking the face of the highest Lord; only indirectly relates the final gift to the Lord's direct agency.
Pairs bracelets and silk in gardens and explicitly contrasts the prior fire-clothing scene with honored adornment.
Completes the carefully measured silver-vessel detail that prepares the silver material reappearing in the bracelets.
Purity is applied to raised pages, offering only a distant analogue to the purifying quality of the drink.
Green surfaces and fine furnishings offer a parallel living-color setting for the green garments, while retaining plant and textile senses.
Its great blessing and dominion form the immediate scene whose outward splendor 76:21 specifies.
Purified pages offer a secondary purity register, not a direct account of clothing or drinking.
Uses the Lord's action in judgment; it only broadly contrasts divine care in 76:21 with destructive judgment.
Names the spring in the immediate drink sequence, supplying the source before the Lord directly gives the purifying drink.
Treats gold bracelets as a demanded badge of rank, a secondary and potentially critical comparison to 76:21's honored silver bracelets.
Contrasts garden rivers and pleasant drink with scalding water that destroys within, clarifying the life-giving versus punitive drink polarity.
Adds near shade and accessible fruit to the prepared garden hospitality surrounding the clothing and drink.
Connects water to earth becoming green, preserving green as living, watered prosperity alongside its garment use.
The denial of coolness and drink supplies a contrary deprivation against 76:21's granted purifying drink.
The prostration scene has no material or contextual contribution to 76:21.
Its overturned upper and lower order is a remote contrary use of elevation, not an explanation of the garments.
Green ears versus dry ones preserve green as a growth-and-decay sign, secondary to its textile sense in 76:21.
Adds reclined ease without sun or bitter cold, defining the stable climate of the same surrounding reward scene.
Repeated appeal to the Lord gives only broad support for the direct divine giver in 76:21.
Silver as worldly architectural display offers a material comparison, without clarifying its transformed use as bracelet.
The later worship command shifts the response to the Lord after the reward scene, a secondary framing for its giver.
Parallels being given a sealed, noble drink; its source sequence supports the continuing drink-service pattern.
Calls descending water purifying, directly supporting the active cleansing register of sharaban tahuran.
Links workers' recompense, forgiveness, and flowing gardens, supporting the reward setting behind 76:21.
The Lord-title is present but gives no specific garment, ornament, or drink evidence.
Green growth opposed to dryness supplies a secondary visual reading of green as vitality subject to reversal.
Mentions bodily cohesion and the reversal of binding within the surah, supporting the bracelet's non-captivity encirclement by contrast.
A contrary forced drink from a scorching spring sharply distinguishes the beneficent purifying drink of 76:21.
Blessing and mercy from the Lord are only a broad analogue to the Lord's direct gift.
States a two-horizon return for good action, supporting the recompense frame later made explicit in 76:22.
Contrasts visible display with enduring divine recompense, helping keep 76:21's splendor within a return-for-deeds frame.
Combines allotted springs, drinking shares, shade, and provision, paralleling organized hospitality without matching 76:21's final gift.
Closes the surah with mercy and painful punishment, preserving the larger contrast between this reward scene and its contrary outcome.
Honor granted after forgiveness offers only a broad analogue to the honorable adornment of 76:21.
Invocation and accounting language do not materially illuminate 76:21.
The revelation statement does not add to the clothing, ornament, drink, or reward sequence.
Mercy from the Lord provides only a general frame for the divine gift.
The green tree yielding fire keeps green open to transformation rather than a fixed textile color alone.
Shows faithful commitment returned as near opening and reward, a secondary analogue to the thanked striving of 76:22.
Names a better divine return for faith and restraint, broadly supporting reward without specifying its forms.
Increase in faith and a surah reference do not clarify the focus verse.
Continued remembrance of the Lord follows the reward passage, keeping the giver-recipient relation active beyond the gifts.
A bad recompense reverses evaluative pretension, supplying a contrary moral-return pattern to 76:21's favorable return.
Describes a pure, palatable drink produced through an interior process, a secondary analogue to inward cleansing through drink.
Gardens and springs supply the broader destination setting for the spring and drink sequence.
Steadfast relation to the Lord and freedom from fear are only remote support for the secure reward scene.
The highest Lord is followed by creation and provision themes, but the link to 76:21 remains general.
Frames a chosen path toward the Lord later in the surah, secondary context for the Lord who grants the final drink.
Explicitly asks whether deeds were repaid, supporting return-for-action; its garment association is only a rejected secondary inference.
Purifying a house for worshippers offers a distant purity and return-place analogy, not a direct parallel.
Names a drink mixture, paralleling the staged cup-mixture-source pattern that culminates in 76:21.
The Lord's knowledge of people gives only broad support for a morally fitting final return.
Dispersion toward trade has no usable connection to the focus verse.
Near fruit in an elevated garden parallels the accessible hospitality around 76:21.
Distinguishes worldly and final recompense, a general return motif without the focus verse's concrete forms.
An elevated garden supports the high, secure reward setting but adds no clothing or drink detail.
The seal and competitive drink context continue a noble beverage register, though not the purification claim itself.
Drinking drawn from an interior source and other benefits offers a secondary pattern of provision entering the recipient.
The elevated garden repeats the setting that makes the surrounding ease and provision intelligible.
A spring drunk by those brought near directly parallels the named springs in the 76 drink sequence.
Treats ornament as a social formation and contested marker, a secondary caution against reducing 76:21 to mere status display.
Crossing a wall has no relevant connection beyond an unrelated root.
Mockery later reverses in the surah; this is only a remote contrary to honored final visibility.
The repeated Lord-address supplies no specific explanatory material for 76:21.
Divine feeding and watering provide a concise source-of-provision parallel to the Lord directly giving drink.
Adornment fashioned into an ineffective idol offers a secondary contrary to honored ornament, not a direct reading.
Dispersion and provisions in a polemical setting do not explain 76:21.
An appeal to the Lord to remove punishment is only a distant contrary to the bestowed reward.
A false claim to lordship contrasts with 76:21's actual divine giver, but adds no positive detail.
Magnifying the Lord broadly frames the following garment-purity command but only indirectly reaches 76:21.
Purity as a condition of touch is a distant and non-identical purity register.
Names gardens with flowing rivers as recompense for what was said, supporting the return and garden context.
Brocade appears as an inner furnishing layer with near fruit, a material and hospitality parallel to the brocade clothing.
The Lord of the house is tied to provision in its local context, but the link is broad.
The Lord's promise of mercy, approval, and abiding bliss supplies a close general frame for the reward scene.
Water access and social circulation offer only a distant service-and-drinking comparison.
A destructive wind over people does not illuminate the focus verse.
Migration toward the Lord is a general directional relation, not evidence for the reward imagery.
The destroyed community has no useful connection to the focus verse.
Judgment by the Lord offers only a broad contrary background to reward.
Debt documentation does not add to the focus verse.
Signs of the Lord's greatness offer only a general theological frame.
The response to mercy and adversity does not clarify 76:21.
The repeated Lord-address supplies no specific clothing, bracelet, or drink evidence.
A torn shirt is a distant garment reference with no meaningful connection to the reward imagery.
The straight path of the Lord is only a broad framework for the surah's final orientation.
Opens the surah's rewarded-drink sequence with a cup and its kafur mixture, making the later direct purifying drink its culmination.
Identifies the earlier drink source as a spring drunk by the servants of God, directly preparing the source-and-service pattern of 76:21.
Adds radiance and joy as rewards, supplying the visible and inward blessed condition surrounding 76:21.
Explicitly joins garden reward with silk, a direct parallel to the textile element of 76:21.
Places the righteous in delight, providing the immediate reward-state in which the related sealed drink appears.
Shows the righteous on couches looking, paralleling the stable, visible ease of the 76 reward scene.
Names radiance recognizable on their faces, closely supporting the outward brightness accompanying 76:21's adornment.
Sets out raised woven couches, a close furnishing parallel to the reclined reward scene before 76:21.
Adds reclining recipients facing one another, matching the communal composure associated with paradisal garments and service.
Names everlasting youths circulating among the recipients, directly paralleling the service sequence of 76:19 and 76:21.
Specifies cups and a cup from a flowing source, closely paralleling the staged cup-source-drink sequence.
Negates harmful effects of the drink, reinforcing its beneficent rather than punitive character.
Places the honored recipients in gardens of bliss, supplying the same reward destination for the drink sequence.
Brings around a cup from a flowing spring, a direct service-and-source parallel to the drink in 76:21.
Describes the drink as white and pleasurable, supporting a favorable sensory register without reducing purification to taste.
Contrasts the drink with harm or loss of awareness, further distinguishing it from destructive drink imagery.
States a successful outcome for the reverent, supplying the reward frame for the following garden hospitality.
Names a filled cup, a concise parallel to the prepared drinking vessels of the 76 passage.
Excludes idle or false speech, supporting the ordered, undisturbed quality of the reward scene.
Begins the contrasting blessed faces in delight, providing a visible reward condition complementary to 76:21.
Places them in a high garden, reinforcing the elevated reward setting.
Names a flowing spring in that garden, directly paralleling the source motif behind the final drink.
Names raised couches, a close furnishing parallel to the reclining scene.
Names cups set out, a direct hospitality parallel to the vessels and drink sequence.
Adds arranged cushions, extending the prepared comfort of the setting.
Adds spread carpets, extending the material ease around the adorned recipients.
Places the successful recipient in a life of satisfaction, supplying the immediate reward state expanded by 76:21.
Commands eating and drinking in satisfaction because of prior deeds, directly joins consumption with earned return.
Places the reverent in gardens and blessing, a close reward-setting parallel.
Names circulating youths likened to protected pearls, directly paralleling the pearl-like attendants of 76:19.
Introduces two gardens for the one who fears standing before the Lord, giving a close reward setting for the material imagery that follows.
Names two flowing springs, directly reinforcing the garden-source pattern of 76:18-21.
Names fruit, palms, and pomegranates together with the two-garden setting, extending the abundant hospitality around the focus verse.
Places the reverent amid shade and springs, a concise parallel to the cool, supplied garden setting.
Shows garden companions occupied in enjoyment on couches, paralleling the settled communal ease before 76:21.
Places the reverent in gardens and springs, supplying a direct destination parallel for the drink source.
Pairs circulated golden dishes and cups with whatever delights the selves and eyes, a close service-and-ornament comparison.
